TOPQ-2020-20.title: Measurement of ttZ total and differential cross sections

resources.description: Archive of full inclusive cross section likelihood in the HS3 JSON format (https://github.com/hep-statistics-serialization-standard/hep-statistics-serialization-standard/releases/tag/v0.2). Detailed explanation of the HS3 JSON format utilisation can be found here - https://opendata.atlas.cern/docs/tutresearch/public_likelihoods/. The workspace was created as the combination of all signal and control regions included in the combined inclusive fit.

Archive of full likelihoods for all differential cross section measurements in the HS3 JSON format (https://github.com/hep-statistics-serialization-standard/hep-statistics-serialization-standard/releases/tag/v0.2). Detailed explanation of the HS3 JSON format utilisation can be found here - https://opendata.atlas.cern/docs/tutresearch/public_likelihoods/. The conversion to the HS3 JSON format was done with ROOT Release 6.30.04 - 2024-01-31 (https://root.cern/releases/release-63004/). Workspaces for regularised observables include regularisation term. The standard uncertainty estimates based on MIGRAD or MINOS result in overestimated uncertainties for likelihoods with regularisation. Due to this the uncertainties in the regularised measurements were estimated from stat-only pseudo-experiments and rankings of nuisance parameters.

For each signal point the background-only model is found in the file named BkgOnly.json. All jsonpatches are contained in the file patchset.json. Each patch is identified in patchset.json by the metadata field "name": "C1N2_Wh_hbb_[m1]_[m2]" where m1 is the mass of both the lightest chargino and the next-to-lightest neutralino (which are assumed to be nearly mass degenerate) and m2 is the mass of the lightest neutralino.
